title: feat(core): flag-gated computer-use section in the cloud session prompt
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** N/A. This is part of the computer-use rollout for cloud sessions ("closing the loop"). Related: #15393 (artifact attach/render), core-platform #3577 (artifact endpoints), core-platform #3581 (sandbox learns its session ID).

### Description

This lets cloud-session agents check their own UI changes. Behind a new `cloud-computer-use` feature flag, the cloud session's system prompt gets a section that tells the agent how to:

- start a virtual display (Xvfb) in the sandbox,
- launch the app in Chromium,
- drive it with xdotool,
- take screenshots with ImageMagick,
- look at the screenshots with `read_files`,
- publish the frames that prove the change with `publish-artifacts --files <list.json> --attach`, so they appear in the user's chat.

This is the "main agent drives it directly" v1 we agreed on. Moving the work into a computer-use subagent and adding a `present` tool for captioned slideshows come later.

**Where it hooks in.** All clients create cloud tasks through the hub daemon's `CloudSessionController`. It builds the system prompt in `buildCloudSessionSystemPrompt` and sends it with `session.create`. Note that on the sandbox hub this prompt *replaces* the normal Cline prompt (`resolveBootstrapSystemPrompt` returns `config.systemPrompt` verbatim). So the new section is written to stand on its own instead of assuming the base prompt's tool guidance.

**Gating.** The section is added only when both of these hold:

1. **The model can see images.** It must be in the bundled `cline` catalog with the `images` capability. Models missing from the catalog are treated as text-only. This is deliberately stricter than `modelSupportsImageInput({})`, which assumes support when capabilities are unknown, so the section never reaches a model whose `read_files` would reject screenshots. The check runs first and is cheap, so non-vision models never hit the flag service.
2. **The flag is on.** This is `isClineAccountFeatureEnabled(FeatureFlag.CLOUD_COMPUTER_USE)`, the same account-scoped PostHog check Composio uses inside the hub daemon, where the client's in-memory flag service isn't available. It's cached for 60s and fails closed. For local development, `CLINE_CLOUD_COMPUTER_USE=1` in the environment the hub daemon inherits turns it on without PostHog.

The controller takes the gate as an injected `isComputerUseEnabled` option. That keeps the controller free of flag and env lookups and makes it easy to test. If the gate throws, the section is left out.

The section is added to both the new-task prompt and the local-to-cloud handoff prompt. It only affects new tasks: existing tasks keep the prompt they were created with.

**Prompt content.** It's adapted from the computer-use spec, with these changes:

- `chromium` instead of `google-chrome`, because the base image is Debian (`node:24-slim`), and window search by `--class chromium`.
- `--no-sandbox` added to the Chromium flags. Chromium's own sandbox doesn't work as a non-root user in this container.
- A tools check first (`command -v Xvfb xdotool import chromium`), with "skip, don't install" if anything is missing. The sandbox runs as `node` without sudo, and the tools arrive via the base image.
- The evidence-file folder (`/tmp/cu-shots/evidence/*.json`) is replaced with `publish-artifacts --attach`, which already exists on cloud-platform's `feat/session-artifacts` branch. The agent describes each published screenshot in its answer, since loose images have no captions yet.

### Test Procedure

- New controller tests:
  - The section is added when the flag is on and the model takes images.
  - It's left out when the flag is off.
  - It's left out when the model isn't in the catalog.
  - It's left out when the gate throws.
- `vitest run src/cloud/controller.test.ts`: 112 passed. `src/hub/server/cloud-session-service.test.ts`: 56 passed.
- `bun run typecheck` in core (dev + smoke) and `tsc` in shared are clean.
- I checked that the new `@cline/llms` import in `cloud/` doesn't reach the desktop webview: its `@cline/core/cloud` imports are type-only.

**Not yet tested end to end.** That needs pieces that haven't merged or deployed:

- core-platform #3581, so the sandbox gets `CLINE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID`.
- cloud-platform `feat/session-artifacts`, which ships the `publish-artifacts` command, after #15393 merges and the SDK is released.
- The computer-use tools in the base image (Marlon).

Until those land, a flagged agent will find the tools missing and skip verification, as the prompt tells it to.

To try it once they land: run desktop with `CLINE_CLOUD_COMPUTER_USE=1`, start a cloud task on a vision model in a repo with a web UI, and ask for a visible change. Published screenshots should appear in the chat.

### Type of Change

-   [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

### Pre-flight Checklist

-   [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs)
-   [x] Tests are passing (`bun test`) and code is formatted and linted (`bun run format && bun run lint`)

### Additional Notes

- The `cloud-computer-use` flag still needs to be created in PostHog. Until then everyone evaluates to off, except dev builds using the env override.
- The first flagged task per minute waits on one PostHog poll before `session.create`. The cache and fail-closed behavior bound this.
- Follow-ups: a `present` tool with title, captions and pass/fail (replacing loose images); a computer-use subagent to keep screenshots out of the main context; artifact rendering outside desktop.

### Related Issue

**Issue:** no GitHub issue; Linear DAT-111. This is a smaller alternative to #15043 that covers just the privacy settings link.

`GET /users/me` now returns `dataPrivacyPath` (for example `/dashboard/account?tab=privacy`), the Cline web app page where users manage Restrict Data Use and Cline Bench preferences. The path comes from the server, so this keeps a bad value from becoming a link to somewhere else.
- **`@cline/core`:** `ClineAccountUser.dataPrivacyPath?: string`.
- **CLI:** the account snapshot builds `privacySettingsUrl` on the environment's `appBaseUrl`, and `/account` adds a **Privacy settings** action that opens it in the browser and leaves the dialog open.

Token refreshes re-fetch `/users/me` for the same user, so without this the new field would never reach the webview.
- **Desktop:** the Account view adds a shield **Privacy settings** button next to **Open dashboard**.

- No `client=` attribution parameter, since the dashboard doesn't read it yet.
- Existing dashboard links aren't migrated or hidden. title: fix(llms): give adaptive-thinking Claude requests the full output budget
body:
## Problem

Adaptive thinking (Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5) counts inside `max_tokens`. When no `maxTokens` is set, the gateway sends `max(32000, 0.3 × model.maxOutputTokens)` — **38,400** for these models. At `--thinking high` the models often think 20–70k tokens on one step, so the call is cut off mid-thought:

- the response has no answer text (finish reason: length), and the thinking is billed and discarded
- the agent then retries with the "output-token limit reached" nudge

In a DeepSWE benchmark campaign (Oct 20, OpenRouter, `--thinking high`), this showed up as ~6-minute calls with 0 output followed by the nudge.

## Fix

For adaptive-thinking requests (`isAdaptiveThinkingRequest`: Claude adaptive-era model id + reasoning enabled), the synthesized default uses the model's **full** advertised output budget (128k) instead of 30% of it.

- still clamped by the context window
- an explicit `maxTokens` still wins
- non-adaptive and non-Claude models are unchanged

## Testing

- New tests in `gateway.test.ts` (128k default, context clamp, explicit override) and `model-facts.test.ts`
- Wire capture: Opus/Sonnet 5.5 now send `max_tokens: 128000`; other models unchanged
- Reran 4 tasks × Opus/Sonnet × 3 on Prime with a 3.0.73 build containing this patch: **0 output-limit truncations** (previously frequent). Calls with 46–77k thinking tokens now complete instead of being cut off.

## Notes for reviewers

- This removes truncation; it does **not** make runs faster. At high effort calls that used to be cut off at ~6 min now finish (some take up to ~12 min). The slowness comes from `high` effort itself and is a separate default question.
- OpenRouter may reserve credit against `max_tokens`; a 128k request could hit "insufficient credits" for low-balance keys. Worth a sanity check.

body:
### Cline Surface

CLI

### Cline Version

3.0.74

### Beta version

- [ ] I am using a beta version of Cline

### What happened?

**Title:** CLI 3.0.74: Switching OpenAI-compatible models drops reasoning metadata and resets reasoning to `none`

**Description**

When switching models using `/model` with an `openai-compatible` provider, Cline resets reasoning to disabled, even when local configuration enables reasoning and declares the model’s supported effort levels.

This causes requests to fail for models that do not support `reasoning_effort: "none"`.

**Environment**

- Cline CLI: 3.0.74
- OS: macOS
- Provider: `openai-compatible`
- Endpoint: a custom OpenAI-compatible gateway

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Configure the provider in `~/.cline/data/settings/providers.json`:

   ```json
   "reasoning": {
     "enabled": true,
     "effort": "medium"
   }
   ```

2. Declare reasoning support for the model in `~/.cline/data/settings/models.json`:

   ```json
   {
     "capabilities": ["streaming", "tools", "images", "reasoning"],
     "reasoningOptions": [
       {
         "type": "effort",
         "values": ["low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"]
       }
     ]
   }
   ```

3. Start Cline and switch models using `/model`.
4. Send a simple message such as `hi`.

**Actual behavior**

Cline changes the persisted provider setting to:

```json
"reasoning": {
  "enabled": false
}
```

The next request sends `reasoning_effort: "none"` and fails. Example error:

```text
Unsupported value: 'none' is not supported with the 'gpt-6-astra' model.
Supported values are: 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh', and 'max'.
```

The issue also occurs with another model that accepts only `low`, `medium`, and `xhigh`.

**Expected behavior**

Switching models should preserve a compatible reasoning setting or prompt for a supported level. Missing metadata should not automatically be interpreted as an instruction to disable reasoning.

**Suspected root cause**

Inspection of the installed CLI bundle shows that the OpenAI-compatible model picker fetches `/models`, extracts only model IDs, and rebuilds entries as `{ id, name }`. When that list is nonempty, it replaces the list derived from `knownModels`.

The rebuilt entries lack `capabilities`, so the picker evaluates `supportsReasoning` as false. The model-selection flow then resets `thinking` to false and clears `reasoningEffort`.

This discards reasoning metadata already present in the local `models.json`, regardless of whether the endpoint returns additional metadata.

**Suggested fix**

Merge discovered model IDs with their corresponding `knownModels` entries, preserving capabilities and reasoning options. If reasoning support is unknown, preserve the existing setting rather than automatically disabling it.

**Workaround**

Starting a new session with an explicit model and effort works:

```bash
cline --model '<model-id>' --thinking medium
```

However, switching models inside the session can reset reasoning again.

### Steps to reproduce

When switching models using /model with an openai-compatible provider, Cline resets reasoning to disabled, even when local configuration enables reasoning and declares the model’s supported effort levels.

This causes requests to fail for models that do not support reasoning_effort: "none".

openai/gpt-6-astra

_No response_

Provider: openai-compatible

title: fix: pass commit search terms to git as arguments, not shell text
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #15377

### Description

Commit search hands the typed query to a shell command, so the shell eats the quotes before `git log` sees them.

`apps/vscode/src/utils/git.ts` interpolated the query into a command string:

```ts
const { stdout } = await execAsync(
	`git log -n 10 --format="..." --date=short ` + `--grep="${query}" --regexp-ignore-case`,
	{ cwd },
)
```

With `"quoted"` as the query, `git` receives `--grep=quoted`, so it also returns commits that only contain the unquoted word. The same pattern was used for the hash fallback (`--author-date-order ${query}`) and for `getCommitInfo()`, where the revision comes from a mention (`@<hash>`) and was also spliced into the command string.

The file already solves this exact problem for file names, and says so:

```ts
// Pass the filename as a separate argv entry (no shell) so names containing
// quotes, `$`, backticks, or spaces can't be interpreted as shell syntax.
```

This PR applies that same pattern to the five remaining call sites: the query and the revision are now single `argv` entries via `execFileAsync("git", [...])`.

### Test Procedure

New cases live in the existing `apps/vscode/src/utils/__tests__/git.test.ts`, next to the untracked-file tests that document the argv rule:

```
$ bun test src/utils/__tests__/git.test.ts
 8 pass
 0 fail
```

Before the change the same file is `6 pass, 2 fail` — the two new cases fail because the quotes are dropped and because the query is executed by the shell. The six pre-existing `getGitDiff` cases pass before and after, so the argv conversion in this file does not regress them.

title: fix(llms): preserve retry billing and actual request size
body:
### Related Issue

N/A — bugs discovered during a prompt-cache audit of the hidden-retry usage path.

### Description

An empty-response retry currently adds token counts from both attempts while retaining only the last attempt's raw billing data. This loses the earlier attempt's reported cost and raw cache-write count. The resulting summed input count is also used as if it were the size of one prompt, which can trigger premature context compaction.

Preserve each attempt's original usage and provider metadata in a private in-process association. Normalize each attempt with the existing provider rules before summing the known billing fields. Two synthetic attempts now report 150 cache-write tokens and cost 0.03 instead of 50 and 0.02, while their standard token totals remain unchanged. Each attempt can use reported cost or pricing fallback; unknown costs do not become a partial reported total.

Pass the last actual request's input size separately in the usage event. Two 1,000-token attempts remain 2,000 billable input tokens but calibrate compaction with 1,000, not 2,000. The optional event field keeps legacy providers working; explicit unknown values clear stale calibration. It also takes the final request of an internal multi-step stream rather than its summed input.

title: fix(llms): back off between in-stream provider retries
body:
## Cause

The AI SDK's `streamRetries` re-dials the moment a provider error part arrives, with no wait between attempts. A provider that is overloaded is still overloaded a few milliseconds later, so all four attempts fail the same way and the user sees the provider's message ("Our servers are currently overloaded. Please try again later.") with a manual Retry button. In telemetry for 4.1.25 (Oct 20–23), 54% of the overload failures that reached users came through this path, and when users retried by hand 2–10 s later, 81% of those retries succeeded.

Two smaller problems on the same path:

- Capacity errors from OpenAI-compatible backends arrive as in-band error parts with no HTTP status. The AI SDK recognises only a few exact messages, so it types these as non-retryable, and our classifier had neither their provider codes nor a message fallback for them.
- The silent retry attempts left no telemetry, so no retry policy could be measured.

## Changes

- `stream-retry-backoff.ts`: `onError` now waits 1 s, 2 s, 4 s (cap 8 s) before the AI SDK's next in-stream attempt; the SDK awaits `onError` before re-dialing. No wait when no stream retry follows (request-start `RetryError`, transport failures, tool-choice violations) or when the failure reproduces on every attempt (credential, context window). Vendors can tune or disable it through `ProviderFactoryResult.streamRetryBackoff`.
- The wait is announced through `emitStatusNotice` ("provider error — retrying in 2s (attempt 2/3)"), which renders as an info row in VS Code and JetBrains and as a status line in the CLI. `GatewayStreamRequest` carries the callback from the agent runtime.
- `error-classification.ts`: provider capacity codes (`server_is_overloaded`, `service_unavailable`, `service_unavailable_error`, `overloaded`, `overloaded_error`, `model_overloaded`) and an `overloaded` message fallback count as retryable when no status is present.
- Telemetry: an `sdk.stream_retry` event per wait; the terminal `sdk.error` carries `streamRetryAttempts` and `streamRetryWaitMs`.
- `sleep` moved out of the empty-response middleware into its own module, shared with the backoff.

Fixes https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/13356 ([CLINE-3015](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/CLINE-3015/error-our-servers-are-currently-overloaded-please-try-again-later)); the same failure was reported in a JetBrains Marketplace review on 2026-08-19.
Refs https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/13606 ([CLINE-3088](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/CLINE-3088/task-aborts-on-transient-api-errors-timeouts-provider-outages-instead)) and [ENG-2350](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/ENG-2350/decision-auto-retry-parity-was-dropped-entirely-restore-or-accept). Request-start failures that exhaust the SDK's own `maxRetries` backoff (the other 46% of overload failures) are out of scope here.

## Tests

```bash
cd sdk/packages/llms && bunx vitest run src/providers/stream-retry-backoff.test.ts src/providers/gateway.test.ts src/providers/error-classification.test.ts src/providers/ai-sdk.stream-retry-backoff.test.ts
```

`ai-sdk.stream-retry-backoff.test.ts` drives the real `ai` package over the OpenAI-compatible wire format: an overloaded error frame, then a successful stream. It asserts that the re-dial waits, that the notice is emitted once, and that the retry's text is what the caller receives.

## Release note

Transient provider errors during a response (such as "servers are currently overloaded") are now retried with a short backoff and shown as a retry notice, instead of failing the request after four immediate attempts.

title: VS Code: extension host OOM in long tasks — subscribeToState re-serializes full state (17 MB) on every streamed event

labels.name: VS Code
labels.description: Issues specific to VS Code

body:
### Cline Surface

VSCode Extension

### Cline Version

4.1.25

### Beta version

- [ ] I am using a beta version of Cline

### What happened?

In long tasks the VS Code (Remote-WSL) extension host dies from V8 heap exhaustion. Cline's panel resets, and reopening the same task brings the crash back within 1–2 minutes, so the task becomes a crash loop.

`remoteagent.log` at each crash:

```
<stderr> FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
Extension Host Process exited with code: null, signal: SIGABRT.
```

The last GC trace lines show the heap at its ~4 GB ceiling (`... -> 4108.5 (4131.5) MB ... allocation failure; scavenge might not succeed`). There were 33 of these exits in 6 days (18 on 10-21, 6 on 10-23, 9 on 10-26).

The Cline output channel shows what fills the heap. While a turn streams, the **entire state** is re-serialized and pushed to the webview about every 0.4–0.6 s:

```
WARN [TelemetryService] Large gRPC response: cline.StateService.subscribeToState size=17.1MB
```

| Extension-host run | `subscribeToState` > 4 MB warnings | Size range | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10-21 | 25,719 | 4.0 – 20.5 MB | 18 OOM exits |
| 10-22/23 | 38,182 | 8.6 – 17.6 MB | 6 OOM exits |
| 10-26 | 4,617 | 16.6 – 17.3 MB | 9 OOM exits |

One run on 10-26 issued 1,194 of these pushes in 41 minutes, **~20 GB of JSON serialized**, and then the host died. After restarting with the same task reopened, it lasted 160 pushes (~70 s).

The task involved has **5,824 messages**: 3,004 tool_use/tool_result pairs and 2,784 thinking blocks. Its `<id>.messages.json` is 17.3 MB, the same size as each push. Context compaction ran (`<id>.compaction.json` exists), but it shrinks only what goes to the model, not the message list sent to the webview, so the push keeps growing with the task's lifetime.

**Where it comes from (4.1.25 `dist/extension.js`, de-minified names approximate):**

```js
// statePostDebouncer = new Debouncer({ debounceMs: STATE_POST_DEBOUNCE_MS /* 50 */, flush: () => this.flushStateToWebview() })

async flushStateToWebview() {
  const state = await this.getStateToPostToWebview()   // includes full clineMessages
  await sendStateUpdate(state)
}

function sendStateUpdate(state) {
  const stateJson = JSON.stringify(state)              // whole state, every time
  captureGrpcResponseSize(Buffer.byteLength(stateJson, "utf8"))
  for (const send of stateSubscribers) send({ stateJson }, false)
}
```

So each flush allocates the full ~17 MB string (≈34 MB as a V8 UTF-16 string if any non-Latin-1 content is present), the object graph built for it, and whatever the postMessage transport copies. That happens at the 50 ms debounce rate, bounded only by how long the stringify takes. Debouncing doesn't help once one flush costs as much as the interval between them.

**What I have not proven:** I don't have a heap snapshot, so I can't say whether these strings are *retained*, as in #15031's JetBrains report (1,111 × 7.25 MB `stateJson` held by a suspended async-generator frame), or are just churn the GC can't keep up with. The symptom matches either way: the heap grows with task length × push rate until it hits the limit.

**Expected:** memory use bounded independently of task length; streaming updates that don't re-send the full message history.

**Suggestions:**
1. Send `partialMessage` / message deltas while streaming, and full state only on structural changes. #4626 proposed state diff sync and was closed.
2. Exclude `clineMessages` (or everything but a window of recent messages) from `subscribeToState`, and let the webview page older messages on demand.
3. At minimum, scale the debounce with payload size, or skip a flush while the previous one is still being serialized or delivered.
4. Let compaction (or an explicit "archive") also trim what the UI holds, so a long task isn't a time bomb when reopened.

**Related:** #15031 (same `stateJson` payload, JetBrains/cline-core, OOM), #12419 (`subscribeToState` 4.1 MB → UI freeze, VS Code 3.86), #4626 (state diff sync proposal), #9541 (heap OOM).

### Steps to reproduce

1. VS Code + Cline 4.1.25 (Remote-WSL here, though nothing in the path looks WSL-specific).
2. Run one long agentic task with a reasoning model. Thinking blocks and tool results inflate the history fastest. Keep going across several context compactions, until the history is a few thousand messages and `<id>.messages.json` is ~10+ MB.
3. Watch the Cline output channel: `Large gRPC response: cline.StateService.subscribeToState size=…MB` appears on nearly every streamed event, growing over time.
4. The extension host eventually exits with `JavaScript heap out of memory` / `SIGABRT`.
5. Reopen the same task from history: the crash comes back within a minute or two of streaming.

Workaround: start a new task. Raising the extension host's heap would only push the crash further out.

### Provider/Model

OpenAI-Compatible (self-hosted llama.cpp / vLLM), Qwen3.8-27B with reasoning enabled. Not provider-specific: the allocation is in the extension's state sync, not the API path.

### Diagnostics

VS Code 1.142.0 (commit 6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1), Remote-WSL; extension host default heap limit (~4 GB).

### System Information

Windows + WSL2 (kernel 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2), 24 cores, 62 GB RAM (the system had plenty of free memory; the limit hit is V8's heap cap, not system RAM).

title: fix(webview): open chat links to local files in the editor
body:
Part of [CLINE-3681](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/CLINE-3681/cline-html-file-can-be-opened-within-cline-app-and-messed-up-whole-ui) (https://github.com/cline/intellij-plugin/issues/1241). The JetBrains side, which stops such a click from replacing the panel, is https://github.com/cline/intellij-plugin/pull/1243.

## Problem

When the model links a local file in a chat message, e.g. `[Open index.html](/Users/me/project/index.html)`, `MarkdownBlock` rendered a plain anchor and left the click to the host. VS Code's webview drops it (only `http`, `https`, `mailto` and `vscode` links are opened), so nothing happened. The JetBrains webview navigated to the resolved URL and lost the panel.

The host cannot do better: by the time the click is a navigation, the href has been through react-markdown's URL sanitising, which blanks `file:` URLs and `C:\` paths as unknown schemes, and through URL resolution against the webview origin, which turns `\\server\share` into `https://server/share`. The webview is the only place where the href the model wrote is still known.

## Change

- `localFileLink(href)` classifies an href as a link to a local file: an absolute POSIX, Windows or UNC path, a `file:` URL, or a scheme-less path relative to the workspace. Web links, other schemes and anchors are left alone. The markdown parser percent-encodes the destination (`C:\x` arrives as `C:%5Cx`, a space as `%20`), so a path is decoded back to what was written; a `file:` URL is passed on as is.
- `MarkdownBlock` keeps those hrefs through `urlTransform` and renders them with a click handler that opens the file through `FileService.openFile` (absolute, `file:`) or `openFileRelativePath` (relative) instead of navigating. The anchor's tooltip names the path. Other links keep their default behaviour.
- `openFile` in `integrations/misc/open-file.ts` turns a `file:` URL into the platform's path with `fileURLToPath`, so drive letters and UNC hosts are interpreted where the file lives. A file that cannot be opened still shows "Could not open file!".

## Testing

- `webview-ui`: `localFileLink.spec.ts` (classification, decoding, `file:` passthrough) and `MarkdownBlock.spec.tsx`, which renders real markdown through the component and checks the href, that the click is prevented, and which RPC is called with what.
- `open-file.test.ts`: absolute path passed through, `file:` URL converted.
- VS Code dev host on macOS: a model reply with five links. Absolute path, relative path and `file:` URL each opened the file in an editor tab; a `C:\...` path reached core as written and showed "Could not open file!" (expected on macOS); the `https` link opened the browser. The panel kept its state.
- JetBrains sandbox (IU 2025.1.7, with https://github.com/cline/intellij-plugin/pull/1243): the same five links; absolute, relative and `file:` open the file through the host bridge, the Windows path shows "Could not open file!", the `https` link goes to the external browser, the panel keeps its state.
- Not run: Windows. The Windows and UNC cases are covered by the unit tests; the path reaches core unchanged and Node resolves it there.

```bash
cd webview-ui && bunx vitest run src/utils/__tests__/localFileLink.spec.ts src/components/common/__tests__/MarkdownBlock.spec.tsx
bun test src/integrations/misc/open-file.test.ts
```

## Release note

Links to local files in Cline's chat open the file in the editor.

title: fix(core): treat a 404/402 from the current-plan endpoint as no plan
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** none filed; found during a post-release telemetry check of desktop 0.0.49 / core 0.2.0.

### Description

#### What telemetry showed

In the first hours after the Oct 26 release, desktop 0.0.49 logged a new error, `no plan history found for user`, from the `cline_account` sidecar command:

- **135 signed-in machines in 3 hours, ~9% of all 0.0.49 machines**, ~2 events each.
- **Zero on 0.0.48.**

It's the only new error type in the release with that kind of reach. It's not a crash, but it inflates desktop error counts and puts the Account view on an error path for free users.

#### Cause

`GET /api/v1/users/me/plan` answers:

- **404** with `{"success":false,"error":"no plan history found for user"}` for anyone who has never had a plan;
- **402** when the plan is unpaid.

Both mean "not subscribed". `ClineAccountService.fetchCurrentUserPlan` (core) didn't distinguish them from a real failure. `request()` throws on any non-2xx, so every caller got a rejected promise.

- **Desktop:** `fetchClinePassModels` in `account-view.tsx` is written to return `null` when there's no plan (`plan?.plan?.entitlements`). It never got the chance, because the invoke rejected first, and the sidecar captured the failure as an `sdk.error`. The call became more prominent in 0.0.49, which is why the error appeared with this release.
- **CLI:** onboarding (`tui/views/onboarding/controller.ts`) already worked around this by string-matching the error message: `message === "no plan found for user"` → unsubscribed. **The API now says `no plan history found for user`**, so that match no longer fires and unsubscribed users land in the ClinePass *error* state instead of *unsubscribed*. That's a second, silent bug with the same root cause.
- **VSCode** was never affected. Its own account service (`apps/vscode/src/sdk/account-service.ts`, `fetchClinePassSubscribedRPC`) maps 404 and 402 to "not subscribed" and has a test for exactly that.

#### Fix

`request()` gains an `absentOnStatus` option: listed statuses resolve `undefined` instead of throwing, checked before the body is parsed. `fetchCurrentUserPlan` passes `[402, 404]`.

The return type was already `Promise<UserCurrentPlan | undefined>`, so every caller already handles `undefined` as "no plan":

- desktop's `fetchClinePassModels` returns `null`;
- CLI onboarding's fulfilled branch sets `"unsubscribed"` when `value?.plan` is empty.

No caller changes are needed. Other failures (401, 5xx, network, timeout) still throw exactly as before.

Why fix it in core rather than in each caller:

- one place, matching VSCode's semantics;
- removes the reliance on the API's error wording that broke the CLI;
- every other `fetchCurrentUserPlan` consumer gets the right behaviour for free.

### Cline Surface

CLI / shared Core MCP client.

Source checkout at `a459f1d04dea030833b558be645011ab739c463b`, `@cline/core` 0.2.0.

MCP tool discovery, before the model request.

Windows, Node.js 24.13.0, Bun 1.4.2.

title: CLI shell tools inherit shared Hub startup environment instead of launching client
body:
Cline CLI 3.0.73 on macOS reuses an existing local Hub. A shell tool invoked by the model then sees the terminal context from whichever client started that Hub.

## Reproduction

1. Launch Cline in terminal A and leave its Hub running.
2. In terminal B export a fresh non-secret canary, launch the interactive CLI, and ask it to run a shell probe comparing that canary and terminal identifiers with terminal B.
3. Compare only presence/equality; do not print credentials or a complete environment.

## Observed

A real model-invoked Python child ran under the pre-existing Hub. Terminal pane/tab/workspace identifiers differed from the new launching shell, TERM_PROGRAM was absent, and five fresh synthetic environment canaries were absent. The expectation was captured from terminal B before launching its TUI; this did not independently capture the TUI process environment.

## Expected

Shell commands receive session-scoped launch context. Two clients sharing the Hub must not inherit each other’s terminal identifiers, and no request may mutate the Hub’s global environment.

## Source diagnosis

Reproduced release: cli-v3.0.73. Confirmed in main dab482348ffd83d1065dfcf8b538076608925a79: HubRuntimeHost.startSession sends no shell environment in session.create; handleSessionCreate starts a Hub-local runtime; the built-in shell executor spawns with a merge of process.env and executor overrides. The daemon therefore supplies its startup environment to later sessions. The released shell executor has the same merge.

Related but different: [the hook lifecycle issue](https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/14961) and [its related PR](https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/15012) concern TaskStart/TaskResume selection from daemon environment. Refreshed issues and PR searches found no exact shell-environment duplicate.

## Scope

No existing Hub was restarted. An isolated data directory reached authentication onboarding, so no isolated authenticated model comparison is claimed.

title: fix(llms): keep Anthropic prompt cache advancing through tool loops
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #15307 (also #15167)

### Description

With the direct Anthropic provider, prompt caching stopped advancing during tool-call loops. Cache reads stayed flat at the size of the first prompt and nothing new was written, so every tool step was billed at the full input rate.

Cause: `buildAnthropicProviderOptions` set the request-level option as `cache_control`. `@ai-sdk/anthropic` strips that key. Only `cacheControl` gets mapped to the top-level `cache_control` that turns on Anthropic's automatic caching, which moves the cache point forward on each turn. Without it, the only breakpoint was the explicit one on the last `user` message. Tool results are sent as `tool` messages, so during a loop that breakpoint stayed on the original prompt.

The Cline and OpenRouter paths were not affected, because the openai-compatible passthrough already sends a top-level `cache_control`.

The fix gives `createEphemeralCacheControl()` an optional key parameter that defaults to the `cache_control` wire field. The Anthropic request-level option now calls it with `"cacheControl"`. All other callers and the per-part markers are unchanged, since the AI SDK accepts both spellings on parts. This is a much smaller alternative to #15174 with the same result.

| Request | Before: cache read / write | After: cache read / write |
|---|---|---|
| Initial prompt | 0 / 3,359 | 0 / 3,361 |
| After 1 tool round | 3,359 / 0 | 3,361 / 3,187 |
| After 2 tool rounds | 3,359 / 0 | 6,548 / 3,188 |
| After 3 tool rounds | 3,359 / 0 | 9,736 / 3,188 |

### Additional Notes

Requests now carry two breakpoints: the explicit one on the last user text and the automatic one. That is within Anthropic's limit of 4. Vertex Claude uses the same `anthropic` options bucket, so it will send the top-level flag as well. I did not test Vertex live.

Adds `cline --cloud "..."` for sending a task straight to Cline Cloud without opening the TUI. - **Model:** the saved cloud pick from the TUI's `/model`, otherwise the local Cline/ClinePass model if the cloud offers it (so `-m` works too), otherwise ClinePass for ClinePass users, otherwise `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`. **Issue:** #14979

### Description

Auto-compaction fired far below the real context window when the char-based token estimate overshot the provider's actual input count.

title: fix(hooks): run UserPromptSubmit hooks for prompts seeded into the runtime
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #14963

### Description

UserPromptSubmit hooks never ran for the user's actual message in CLI and desktop sessions.

Two different paths deliver the prompt to `AgentRuntime`:

1. A directly driven runtime gets the prompt as `run(input)` and emits it as `message-added`.
2. Orchestrated sessions (what the CLI and desktop use) append the user message to the conversation, seed it into `initialMessages`, and call `run("")`. No `message-added` event fires for that prompt.

The file hook layer only dispatched `prompt_submit` from `message-added`, so path 2 never fired the hook. The VS Code hooks adapter already handles this by scanning the `beforeRun` snapshot; this change does the same at the core file-hook layer and in the CLI's in-process hook dispatcher.

Changes:

- `createHookConfigFileHooks` now installs `beforeRun` when prompt_submit hooks exist and scans the snapshot for the latest user message that is not marked `displayRole: "system"`, dispatching `prompt_submit` there. If a run-start hook cancels the run, the prompt hook is skipped, matching the extension.
- `onEvent` keeps handling `message-added` for directly driven runtimes. Dispatched message ids are tracked so a `continue()` run, whose snapshot still contains earlier prompts, does not re-fire them.
- The audit hook layer records the same prompt_submit dispatch so `hooks.jsonl` reflects what the file hooks actually ran.
- Runtime-generated user-role reminders (completion-tool reminder, completion policy reminders, max-tokens recovery nudge, unexpected-turn continuation) are now marked `displayRole: "system"` so the snapshot scan does not mistake them for user prompts.
- The CLI's in-process hook dispatcher in `apps/cli/src/utils/hooks.ts` gets the same snapshot scan and dedup.

- `sdk/packages/core`: `bun vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/hooks/hook-file-hooks.test.ts` passes (29 tests). New coverage: a prompt seeded in the `beforeRun` snapshot dispatches `prompt_submit` with the prompt text; a snapshot holding only a `displayRole: "system"` user message dispatches nothing; repeated `beforeRun` calls with the same snapshot dispatch exactly once.
- `apps/cli`: `bun vitest run src/utils/hooks.test.ts` passes (8 tests), including a seeded-snapshot dispatch plus dedup check.
- `sdk/packages/agents`: `bun vitest run src/agent-runtime.test.ts` passes (152 tests); reminder metadata changes do not alter existing behavior.

title: cli: publish musl builds for Linux
body:
Refs #15271.

## What

Adds musl Linux to the CLI's build matrix and publishes two more platform packages:

- `@cline/cli-linux-x64-musl`
- `@cline/cli-linux-arm64-musl`

The glibc Linux packages additionally get `"libc": ["glibc"]`, and the musl ones
`"libc": ["musl"]`, so npm's libc-aware optional dependency resolution
(npm >= 10.4) installs the right binary on each host instead of pulling in a
glibc build that dies in the loader.

## Why it was more than one line

Bun compiles these targets from any host (`bun-linux-{x64,arm64}-musl`), and
`@opentui/core` already ships `core-linux-{x64,arm64}-musl`. Two things were
still missing:

1. **OpenTUI picks its native library at runtime** from `OPENTUI_LIBC`,
   defaulting to glibc. A musl binary therefore extracted and loaded the glibc
   `.so` and failed with `Error loading shared library ld-linux-x86-64.so.2`.
   The target's libc is now baked in with a `define`, which also lets Bun
   tree-shake the variant it will never load (156 MB -> 143 MB).
2. **The npm wrapper and `postinstall.mjs` hard-code**
   `@cline/cli-<os>-<arch>`. Both now append `-musl` when the running Node has
   no glibc runtime, using Node's diagnostic report.

## Testing

Built all eight targets with the patched script (`bun script/build.ts
--install-native-variants --skip-sdk-build`, ~2 minutes) and ran the
`@cline/cli-linux-x64-musl` binary on **OpenWrt 24.10.8 / x86_64 / musl**
(`libstdcpp6` installed, which is the only extra system dependency — Bun's
musl runtime links `libstdc++.so.6`):

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `cline --version` | `3.0.73`, 0.8 s |
| `cline hub start` / `status` / `stop` | running, coreVersion `0.2.0` |
| TUI (opentui render library) | renders the welcome screen |
| peak RSS (TUI) | ~230 MB |

`bun biome check` and `bun -F @cline/cli typecheck` pass. The arm64 musl
binary builds and links against `/lib/ld-musl-aarch64.so.1`, but I have not
run it on aarch64 hardware yet.

Note for the release workflow: musl binaries still need `libstdc++` on the
target system (a 643 KB package on OpenWrt). If you would rather not carry that
dependency, it can be documented or handled in a follow-up — the build itself
does not change.

- In Cloud mode, `/model` (and "Change model" in `Ctrl+P`) opens a "Select Cloud Model" picker laid out like the Settings model picker: `Provider: ClinePass (tab to change provider)` above a searchable list of that provider's models. `Tab` opens a "Select Cloud Provider" list with the cloud billing catalogs the desktop app offers (ClinePass, Cline Usage-Billing, ClineFree). The pick shows on the status bar (for example `ClinePass: kimi-k3.1-pro`), is used to create the session, and is sent with every message, so you can switch models mid-session.
- Cloud model choice, matching VS Code (#15302): an explicit `/model` pick in Cloud mode is saved and wins while the cloud catalog offers it. Without one, the default is recomputed each time: your local Cline or ClinePass model if the cloud catalog offers it, otherwise ClinePass if your selected local provider is ClinePass, otherwise Cline's default usage-billed model (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`). Defaults are never saved, so they follow later changes to your local model or provider.
- The first time you pick Cloud, a setup dialog walks through signing in to Cline and connecting GitHub, reusing the extension's wording. After that, a "Run in Cline Cloud" picker opens. It's laid out like Select Model: `Repository: x (tab to change repository)` above a searchable branch list. It defaults to this folder's `origin` repo and to the default or current branch, and branch search runs on the server.
- When you submit, the status row shows the sandbox phases (Starting sandbox, Cloning repository, Starting agent), then Working or Ready in Cline Cloud. The transcript streams in from the cloud session, and follow-up messages go to the same session.
- Once a cloud session starts, the target is locked. `Ctrl+L` returns to a fresh chat with the repo still selected.

- `runtime/interactive/cloud-sessions.ts` connects a `HubCloudSessionClient` (from `@cline/core/cloud`, #15205) to the shared Hub. The Hub owns credentials, provisioning and sandbox connections.
- `tui/hooks/use-cloud-sessions.tsx` holds the target, repo and model selection, setup flow, create/send/abort, and snapshot projection. The transcript renders from cloud snapshots via the existing `hydrateSessionMessages`, so reconnects and rehydration need no extra handling.

## Summary

`getInstallationInfo` resolves the package manager from the wrapper path, but the npx patterns only match the macOS/Linux npm cache layout (`~/.npm/_npx/...`). On Windows the npx cache lives at `%LocalAppData%\npm-cache\_npx\...`, which does not contain the `/npm/_npx` substring, so `npx cline` falls through to the `/node_modules/` check and is misdetected as a global **npm** install.

Consequences for Windows `npx cline` users:

- `cline update` runs `npm update -g cline --tag latest --min-release-age=0`, creating a global npm installation the user never asked for.
- The exit-time auto update (`applyDeferredUpdate`) can run that same global install silently in the background once no other CLI is attached to the hub.
- `getPreferredKanbanInstaller` resolves to `"npm"`, so kanban installs are also pointed at npm.

On macOS/Linux detection correctly returns `NPX` (no update command, auto update skipped), so this is a Windows-only divergence.

## Changes

- Add `/npm-cache/_npx` to the npx detection patterns in `getInstallationInfo` (one extra condition, same style as the existing alternatives).
- Add vitest cases for both the macOS `.npm/_npx` layout (existing behavior, previously untested) and the Windows `npm-cache/_npx` layout.

## Testing

- Detection matrix verified standalone: Windows npx caches (npm v6/v7 layouts) flip `NPM` -> `NPX`; global npm, pnpm-global Windows, and macOS npx detections are unchanged.
- The two added vitest cases in `update.test.ts` run in CI.

Related context: #13115 (update failure on global npm installs) and #12224 (bun global detection) are the same detection area but distinct issues. Yarn Classic global installs on Windows (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Yarn\...`, capital Y) also miss the `/yarn/global` pattern; left out to keep this change minimal, happy to follow up if preferred.

title: Broken Anthropic prompt caching on tool calls in v4.1.25 ("Next" engine) resulting in cost spikes.

labels.description: Issues specific to VS Code

body:
### Cline Surface

VSCode Extension

### Cline Version

4.1.25

### Beta version

- [ ] I am using a beta version of Cline

### What happened?

I’ve been experiencing massive API cost spikes since migrating to the "Next" engine in v4.1.25. After comparing `.messages.json` logs from the Next engine against my older `api_conversation_history.json` logs from the Legacy engine, I found a major implementation flaw with how Prompt Caching is handled.

The "Next" engine fails to advance `cache_control` breakpoints during autonomous tool-call loops.

When running the **Steps to reproduce** test, there are 2 cases:

**Expected Behavior (Legacy Engine v4.0.12):**
The cache advances dynamically with each tool call. `cacheWriteTokens` registers a spike whenever a new file is read, and `cacheReadTokens` grows steadily on each subsequent automated turn (e.g., 10k → 12k → 15k). The conversation tail is successfully cached.

**Actual Behavior (Next Engine v4.1.25):**
The prompt cache does not advance during the autonomous loop. `cacheReadTokens` permanently flatlines at the initial system prefix size (~15k), and `cacheWriteTokens` stays at 0 for all subsequent automated turns.

**Why this is happening:**
Anthropic's API requires explicit `{"cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}` tags on the latest messages to move the cache pointer forward. The "Next" engine appears to only attach these breakpoints to literal user messages, completely abandoning the conversation tail during autonomous loops. Because of this, a 70k context task bills the full $2.00/M input rate on every single autonomous step instead of the $0.10/M cached rate.

Reverting to v4.0.12 (Legacy) immediately fixes the issue and restores cheap tool-call loops. Can we get the `cache_control` breakpoints properly applied to tool results in the Next engine?



### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a task that requires multiple sequential tool calls (e.g., "read file A, then file B, then file C").
2. Check the Anthropic API token metrics for the autonomous steps.

title: CLI --timeout accepts values like "10m" as seconds, and schedule turns invalid timeouts into 1 second

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Cline CLI

body:
### Cline Surface

CLI

### Cline Version

CLI 3.0.73 (main @ 16bade5)

### Beta version

- [ ] I am using a beta version of Cline

### What happened?

Numeric CLI flags are parsed with `Number.parseInt`, which reads the leading digits and ignores the rest. Values that should be rejected are accepted with a different meaning, and nothing warns about it.

**1. `cline --timeout` / `--retries`** (`apps/cli/src/commands/program.ts`)

The code already rejects bad values (`main.ts` prints `invalid timeout "…" (expected integer >= 1)`), but only when the value has no leading digits:

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `--timeout 10m` | 10-second timeout |
| `--timeout 1.5` | 1-second timeout |
| `--timeout 1e3` | 1-second timeout |
| `--timeout abc` | rejected (correct) |
| `--retries 3x` | 3 retries |

**2. `cline schedule create/update --timeout`** (`apps/cli/src/commands/schedule/common.ts`, `toPositiveInt(opts.timeout, 1)`)

This is worse, because anything that doesn't parse to a positive integer silently falls back to **1 second**:

| Input | Stored timeout |
|---|---|
| `--timeout 600` | 600 s |
| `--timeout 30m` | 30 s |
| `--timeout 1h` | 1 s |
| `--timeout abc` | 1 s |
| `--timeout 0` | 1 s |

Scheduled runs are unattended, so a schedule created with `--timeout 1h` times out on every run, and the user isn't there to see why.

**Expected:** a value that isn't a whole number of seconds is rejected with a clear error, like `--timeout abc` already is for the main command, rather than being truncated or replaced with 1.

**Possible fix:** check the whole string first (e.g. `/^\d+$/.test(raw)`), then `Number(raw)`. For `schedule`, throw an `InvalidArgumentError` instead of falling back to 1. `--retries`, `schedule --max-parallel` and `history --limit` use the same pattern and could share one helper.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `cline -t 10m "count slowly to 100"`. The intent is 10 minutes, but the value is parsed as 10 seconds, so the run stops early (`run timed out after 10s`). No warning about the flag is shown.


2. `cline schedule create test --cron "0 * * * *" --prompt "hi" --workspace . --timeout 1h`. The schedule is saved with a 1-second timeout.

Shown directly through the parsers (run with `bun --conditions=development` from `apps/cli`):

```ts
import { commanderToParsedArgs, createProgram } from "./src/commands/program";
import { toPositiveInt } from "./src/commands/schedule/common";

const p = createProgram();
p.exitOverride();
p.action(() => {});
p.parse(["node", "cline", "--timeout", "10m", "hello"]);
console.log(commanderToParsedArgs(p).timeoutSeconds); // 10

console.log(toPositiveInt("1h", 1)); // 1
console.log(toPositiveInt("abc", 1)); // 1
```

### Provider/Model

N/A (bug is in command-line argument parsing; happens before any model is called)

### Diagnostics

Reproduced from source: cline/cline main @ 16bade5, apps/cli version 3.0.73.

### System Information

OS: Linux (reproduced from source with Bun / Node 22)
Hardware: not relevant (argument parsing bug)

### Related Issue

**Issue:** #15284

### Description

With an `openai-compatible` provider, the `/model` picker lists no models when the API key is supplied via the `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable instead of being stored in `providers.json`. It works when the key is in `providers.json`.

The fallback is gated on `providerId === "openai-compatible"` so the OpenAI key is never sent to an unrelated provider. The helper was extracted into its own module so it can be unit tested without the TUI hook (verbatim move, no behavior change beyond the fallback).

- Added `openai-compatible-models.test.ts` with three cases: the env-key fallback sends `Authorization: Bearer <OPENAI_API_KEY>`; a non-openai-compatible provider does not receive the env key; a stored `apiKey` takes precedence over the env var.

title: Allow an openai-compatible provider's key to come from a command, like Claude Code's apiKeyHelper
body:
The CLI reads a provider's API key once at launch, from settings or the environment. A deployment whose credential is rotated — a gateway that issues short-lived keys, a secret manager, a local helper — then needs its configuration edited or the process restarted before a new key is used.

**Proposal.** Add a credential-command setting to the `openai-compatible` provider, starting with the CLI and followed by the Desktop app and the SDK. Call it `keyCommand`: a shell command that prints the current key on stdout.

- When it is set, Cline runs it and uses the trimmed stdout as the bearer key.
- Run it at launch, and again when the provider answers 401, so a rotated key is picked up inside a session.
- The command runs as the user. The key it prints is never stored in settings or written to disk.
- When the setting is absent, behaviour is unchanged; a static key or the environment variable still wins as today.

**Prior art.** Claude Code's `apiKeyHelper` is the same shape: a command the harness runs to obtain the current credential.

**Acceptance.**
- With `keyCommand` set, a session starts with no key in settings and none in the environment, using the command's output.
- Changing what the command prints is picked up without restarting Cline, at the next 401 at the latest.
- The command's output is never logged or persisted.
- The static-key and environment paths behave exactly as before.

Happy to try a branch if the shape looks right.

title: fix(llms): explain provider timeouts in plain words and record where they happened
body:
## What was wrong

When a model provider accepts a request and then sends nothing, the run sits for 5 minutes until Bun's built-in fetch timeout gives up. The user then sees only "The operation timed out.", which doesn't say what happened or what to do. Telemetry records the same raw text, so there is no easy way to tell a provider that never started replying from one that stopped partway through.

In the last 7 days, the CLI and Desktop logged about 4,400 of these timeouts, almost all on cheap or free models.

## What this changes

- **Plain message.** When a timeout ends the run, the user sees either "The model provider stopped responding before it started its reply." or "The model provider stopped responding partway through its reply.", followed by "Send a message to continue, or switch models if this keeps happening."
- **Telemetry.** `sdk.error` gets a `timeoutPhase` field (`before_reply` or `mid_reply`), so a model or provider that starts going silent can be spotted and alerted on. The raw error text in telemetry is unchanged.

Retry decisions and time limits are unchanged: a timeout still ends the run after the same wait.

## How it was tested

- New gateway tests make the stream throw Bun's `TimeoutError`, once before any content and once after some text. They check the message the user sees, the raw error text and `timeoutPhase` in `sdk.error`, and that the error is still not retried.
- An end-to-end run through a real hub against a fake provider that goes silent, before replying and partway through, shows the new messages after the usual 300-second wait. Normal replies and dropped connections behave as before.

title: CLI: publish musl Linux builds (bun-linux-x64-musl / bun-linux-arm64-musl)
body:
## Summary

The CLI installs successfully on musl-based Linux, but cannot run: every published Linux binary is glibc-only. Please publish two more platform packages built for musl:

- `@cline/cli-linux-x64-musl`
- `@cline/cli-linux-arm64-musl`

and teach the `cline` wrapper and `postinstall.mjs` to select them.

## Environment

- Cline CLI `3.0.73` (`npm install -g cline`)
- OpenWrt 24.10.8 x86_64 (musl 1.2.x), also reproducible on OpenWrt 25.12
- The same applies to Alpine Linux (very common for containers and CI) and other musl distributions

## What happens today

`npm install -g cline@3.0.73` on a musl system installs the wrapper and `@cline/cli-linux-x64` (the platform packages carry `os`/`cpu` but no `libc` field, so npm selects the glibc package). Running `cline` then fails to spawn the platform binary with `ENOENT`:

- `@cline/cli-linux-x64`'s `bin/cline` is a Bun-compiled ELF with interpreter `/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2` and `NEEDED` entries for `libc.so.6`, `libpthread.so.0`, `libdl.so.2` and `libm.so.6`.
- A musl system has no `/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2`, so `execve` fails before any Cline code runs.

The wrappers cannot fall back to another package even if one existed: in the published 3.0.73 `cline` package, `bin/cline` builds the name as

```js
const base = "@cline/cli-" + platform + "-" + arch;
```

and `postinstall.mjs` does the same:

```js
const packageName = `@cline/cli-${platform}-${arch}`;
```

There is no libc component in the name, so musl resolves to the glibc package.

## Why compatibility layers are not a workaround

- `gcompat` (glibc-on-musl) is not in OpenWrt's package feeds for 24.10 or 25.12. Alpine ships it, but it is a partial glibc ABI and running Bun-compiled glibc binaries under it is unreliable, so it is not a substitute for a real musl build.
- Asking users on musl to run a glibc container is a large workaround for something that is a compile-target change.

## Proposed change

`apps/cli/DISTRIBUTION.md` says each target is produced with `bun build --compile --target bun-{os}-{arch}`, and Bun supports musl targets directly:

- `bun-linux-x64-musl`
- `bun-linux-arm64-musl`

(https://bun.sh/docs/bundler/executables)

So this is two additional build targets, not a port.

1. **Build/publish** (`script/build.ts`, `script/publish-npm.ts`): produce `@cline/cli-linux-x64-musl` and `@cline/cli-linux-arm64-musl` with `"os": ["linux"], "cpu": ["x64"|"arm64"], "libc": ["musl"]`, and add `"libc": ["glibc"]` to the existing Linux packages. npm honours the `libc` field when selecting optional dependencies (this is how `@rollup/rollup-linux-x64-musl` and `@img/sharp-linuxmusl-x64` ship), so only the matching package is installed.
2. **Wrapper** (`package/bin/cline` and `postinstall.mjs` in the `cline` package): append `-musl` on musl systems. `detect-libc` or a `process.report` check works:

```js
const isMusl = (() => {
  try { return !process.report.getReport().header.glibcVersionRuntime } catch { return false }
})();
const suffix = platform === "linux" && isMusl ? "-musl" : "";
const base = `@cline/cli-${platform}-${arch}${suffix}`;
```

(The wrapper itself runs on Node, which exists on musl distributions such as Alpine and OpenWrt, so only the compiled binary needs the musl variant.)

## Help offered

I maintain the [luci-app-fcc](https://github.com/Arthur97172/luci-app-fcc) LuCI package that installs the Cline CLI on OpenWrt routers and currently has to exclude Cline on musl. I can test an x64 musl build on OpenWrt 24.10 and 25.12 and report back, and I am happy to open a PR for the build/packaging/wrapper changes if you want to take this.

title: fix(core): stop re-cutting read_files results to the 8k tool-result cap
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** Fixes #13923 · [CLINE-3196](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/CLINE-3196)

Related: #13263 (the `read_files` half of it), #14257 (closed in favour of this change).

### Description

A file read passes through two caps that were set independently and never matched up:

- `read_files` bounds its own output at 2000 lines / ~48k characters and tells the model so, both in the tool description and in a per-read footer (`[Showing lines 1-424 of 1500. Use start_line/end_line to read other sections.]`).
- `MessageBuilder` then cuts **every** tool result to 8k characters on the way to the provider, middle-out, with a bare `...[truncated N chars]...` marker.

So a read the model was just told it received in full reaches it ~17% intact. Ranged reads that fit the tool cap carry no footer at all, so there the cut is the only signal — a 345-line range comes back as its first and last ~60 lines. Models respond by paging in ever smaller slices, concluding the tool is broken, and falling back to `cat`/`sed` through the shell (see the issue and the Discord report that prompted this).

The 8k tool-result cap was introduced for command and MCP output, where it was measured; file reads already had a purpose-built cap with paging guidance. `MessageBuilder` also already has a looser 50k cap for file content — user `file` attachments were routed to it precisely so the aggressive tool-result cap would not mutilate them. This change routes read-tool results to that same cap. A well-formed read (≤ ~48.1k with line-number prefixes and footer) is now never re-cut; the 50k cap remains a backstop for a custom read executor that ignores the tool's bounds. Nothing else moves: `run_commands`, search, MCP and custom tools keep the 8k cap; the aggregate 6MB request budget and the stale-read rewrite still bound history growth.

A `maxToolResultChars` that is configured explicitly (option or `CLINE_MESSAGE_BUILDER_MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS`) keeps its documented meaning of capping every tool result, so it also bounds reads: the read cap is `min(50k, explicit cap)`, and the 50k default only applies when no override is set.

Two existing tests encoded the 8k cut on read fixtures and were adjusted to keep their intent (image siblings preserved while text truncates; stale-read batching counts provider-bound bytes, not raw history bytes) under the read cap.

### Test Procedure

- New unit tests in `message-builder.test.ts` ("read-result cap"): a tool-capped 48k `read_files` window is sent whole (structured and string content), a 60k read result is still cut at the file-content cap, `run_commands` output is still cut at 8k, and an explicit `maxToolResultChars` — as an option and via the env var — still bounds reads while an empty environment keeps the 50k default. The first two fail on `main`.
- New `message-builder.read-files.test.ts` drives the real `read_files` tool through `MessageBuilder` with a 751-line markdown file — whole file, lines 55-400 and lines 110-230, i.e. the reads from the report — plus a batched two-file read, and asserts what the tool returned is what the provider request carries. The single-file cases fail on `main` (7,967 / 7,895 / 7,955 chars of 47,384 / 23,648 / 8,280 reach the model).
- `@cline/core` unit suite, `tsc` and Biome green.

Workaround for affected users until this ships: `CLINE_MESSAGE_BUILDER_MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS=50000` in the environment the IDE/CLI starts from (raises the cap for every tool, not only reads).

body:
### Cline Surface

JetBrains Plugin

### Cline Version

4.1.23

### Beta version

- [ ] I am using a beta version of Cline

### What happened?

**Environment**
- Cline JetBrains plugin, core 2.0.7
- PyCharm Professional 2026.2, Windows 10 Pro FR
- Laptop, keyboard + touchpad only (no mouse wheel)
- [Not tested on the VS Code extension]

**Problem**
In a long conversation, any attempt to scroll up (ArrowUp / PageUp / Home on the keyboard, or touchpad) is immediately undone: the view snaps back to the bottom. This also happens **after streaming has finished**, so it is not only an "auto-follow while streaming" issue. Long responses can only be read from their end, and earlier messages are effectively unreachable.

**Expected**
Auto-scroll should follow new content only while the user is already at the bottom. Once the user scrolls up, the view should stay where they put it until they scroll back down (or send a message).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a conversation with a long response or many messages.
2. Scroll up with the keyboard or touchpad.
3. The view returns to the bottom.

**Findings**
The scroll container is `[data-virtuoso-scroller="true"]`. The behavior stops completely if programmatic scrolling on that element is blocked while the user has scrolled up: overriding `Element.prototype.scrollTo`, `scrollBy`, `scrollIntoView` and the `scrollTop` setter to no-op when the element is "user-locked" fixes it. So the snap-back comes from programmatic scroll calls, not from the browser. I have not identified which component triggers them.

Workaround (prepended to `webview-ui/build/assets/index.js`):
[fix-scroll.js](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33768585/fix-scroll.js)

To apply fix-scroll.js, I used this powershell script:
```
$dir = "$env:APPDATA\JetBrains\PyCharm2026.2\plugins\cline\core\2.0.7\extension\webview-ui\build\assets"
Copy-Item "$dir\index.js" "$dir\index.js.bak"
```

title: feat(core): import Cursor sessions into Cline Desktop
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** https://github.com/cline/cline/discussions/15252

### Description

Cline Desktop can import past sessions from Claude Code, Codex and opencode. This adds Cursor.

The new `cursor` adapter in `@cline/core` reads Cursor's local chat store (`User/globalStorage/state.vscdb`). It lists each conversation once, using Cursor's composer id as the source id, so the existing dedup works. Tool calls keep their ids and results, and timestamps, model, workspace folder and git branch carry over. Drafts, subagents, empty conversations and Claude Code mirrors are skipped.

The database is only ever opened read-only. When Cursor is closed it uses an immutable open, so no side files are created. While Cursor is running it acts as a normal read-only reader of the live WAL, and only when Cursor's own `-wal` and `-shm` already exist. In any other state it fails with a clear message rather than risk creating files. Reads go through a fixed list of JSON fields, so Cursor's stored secrets and encryption keys are never read. Malformed rows are skipped instead of hiding every session.

Cursor is also listed in the desktop import dialog, Settings → Import and the docs.

Credit to @treeuri: #13910 explored Cursor's agent-transcript files. Those transcripts have no tool ids, results or timestamps, so this PR reads the store instead. A transcript fallback for sessions that aren't in the store is a planned follow-up.

### Test Procedure

- `vitest src/services/session-import`: 55 tests. They use synthetic stores and cover:
  - the live-WAL reader and the no-WAL immutable path, including a Bun subprocess run
  - no side files on a corrupt store or a `-wal` without `-shm`
  - write rejection, and the source file staying byte-identical
  - planted fake secrets never being read
  - malformed rows, filters, mapping, turn boundaries, per-turn models and safe truncation
  - the cwd chain and service dedup
- Desktop: session-import, import-view and sessions-view tests (27). `@cline/core` typechecks at every commit; `@cline/code` at HEAD.
- Real Cursor 3.22 store (counts only, nothing imported): 123 sessions discovered, 123 converted with 0 errors. Discovery takes about 90 ms and the slowest conversion 33 ms. Cursor's database hash, mtime and folder listing were unchanged afterwards.
- Desktop dev app with a synthetic Cursor home: Cursor shows in Settings → Import and in the dialog, and an imported session opens with the "Imported from Cursor" notice.

title: feat(checkpoints): explain why a message has no workspace checkpoint
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #XXXX

### Description

Hovering a disabled Reset Code button now explains why the message has no workspace checkpoint, and usually what to do about it. For example: "This git repository has no commits yet, so no checkpoint was taken. Make an initial commit to enable checkpoints." Previously every cause showed the same generic sentence.

Core now records one outcome for each user turn: either a checkpoint, or a `CheckpointFailure` whose `errorMessage` is written for the user. Hosts show that text unchanged, so adding a cause or rewording one needs no proto or webview change. The recorded causes are:

- the workspace isn't a git repository
- the repository has no commits yet (`git init` alone isn't enough, because checkpoints snapshot against `HEAD`)
- git isn't installed
- a snapshot or a custom `createCheckpoint` failed; a callback that throws is recorded, then rethrown as before

Pure bookkeeping lives in `session/checkpoint-records.ts`. `resolveRunCheckpoint(session, runCount)` is the single rule that Reset Code availability, edit-and-regenerate and core restore all use:

- If the turn has a checkpoint, it is used.
- If the turn has a recorded failure, it reports that failure and won't restore files. It no longer falls back to an older checkpoint, which would have quietly undone later turns' work as well.
- Turns with no record, from older sessions or from runs with checkpoints off, fall back to the nearest earlier checkpoint as before. If there is none, the controller asks core to check the current workspace for an explanation.

Restored and edited sessions carry their recorded failures forward alongside their checkpoints. Failures are never pruned, since each one is what stops its run from falling back. A chat-only restore leaves files alone, so a failed snapshot doesn't block it. Desktop edit-forks use the same rule, and `sdk/ARCHITECTURE.md` describes the record.

`checkpointExistsForMessage` now returns `{ exists, errorMessage }`. A shared conversion turns that into `{ exists: true } | { exists: false; errorMessage: string | undefined }` on both sides. The webview decides what to show:

- If a checkpoint exists, Reset Code is enabled, whatever the Checkpoints setting.
- If there is no checkpoint and checkpoints are currently disabled, it shows the existing Enable Checkpoints popover with the Settings link.
- Otherwise it shows the backend's explanation, or the old generic sentence if there is none.

Because the setting is read on every render, the explanation updates when the user enables checkpoints, without another lookup.

title: fix(core): accept 7 as Sunday in cron day-of-week
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #15245

### Description

Standard cron accepts both `0` and `7` for Sunday in the day-of-week field. The schedule parser only accepted `0-6`, so expressions such as `0 9 * * 7` or `0 9 * * 5-7` failed with `Invalid cron value "7" for range [0-6]`. This blocks `cline schedule create`, `schedule update` and `*.cron.md` specs that use that common form.

`parseCron` now parses the day-of-week field over `0-7` and maps `7` to `0`, so `7` alone, ranges ending in `7` and steps over `*` all resolve to the same weekday set as standard cron. Other fields are unchanged.
